notes: Epic -> Story -> Slice backlog. Vertical slices, each a demo-able increment (Protocol 0.8). Each slice id is stable and used as the tasks/<slice-id>.md filename and as the ACOS bridge slice id. parent_story on each slice maps it to its story; parent_epic maps story to epic. Effort S/M/L. dependency_order is the global build order. Demos D0-D3 (plan.md sec 4).

epics.title: Diagnostics + validation (problem-before-solution)
epics.description: Confirm symptoms/unknowns, lock the Python 3 stdlib decision, and lock the stubbed-access ground rules before any solution build. Validates hypothesis H1 (aggregation/units/currency/truncation dominate the trust failure, not raw text fabrication).

epics.title: Skill scaffold + ACOS integration
epics.description: Skill loader, NL command surface, evidence-bundle wiring, config surface, and the tier-router entry point.

epics.title: Hypercore client/adapter contract + fixture/mock backend (stubbed-until-access)
epics.description: Read-only adapter contract; FixtureBackend active now; LiveBackend stubbed/TODO; NoLiveDataError + is_live() degradation.

epics.title: Two-tier data model + raw-response cache
epics.description: Tier-1 RawApiResponse source-of-truth cache + Tier-2 NormalizedAnswerRecord derived view with per-field back-pointers.

epics.title: Provenance-binding engine (refuse-on-missing)
epics.description: Bind every delivered value to endpoint+request_params+timestamp+json_field_path+raw_response_id; refuse delivery when binding is missing.

epics.title: Deterministic gate suite
epics.description: schema validation, pagination-completeness, freshness window, cross-field reconciliation, unit/currency normalization, single-source confidence cap <= 0.7.

epics.title: Adversarial multi-model consensus orchestrator
epics.description: Dispatch N blind general-purpose agents via Task() (subscription-only); substance consensus; bounded re-dispatch then escalate; never a silent pick.

epics.title: NL question -> verified report/table/dataset pipeline + provenance/confidence display
epics.description: End-to-end orchestration in SKILL.md: question -> plan -> fetch -> verify -> answer; answer/refusal/no-live-data envelopes with mandatory provenance + confidence + freshness + tier.

epics.title: Downstream trusted-input feed formats for consumer skills
epics.description: report/table/dataset (JSON/CSV) feed format with embedded per-value provenance/confidence + manifest, consumable by acos-dataroom-v2 / acos-financial-statement / prospectus / legal-analyst.

epics.title: Security / PII / GDPR + secret handling + read-only enforcement hardening
epics.description: PII-scrubbed logs/evidence; env/secret-store credentials; structural read-only guard; completeness/freshness/schema-drift hardening.

stories.title: As the team, confirm the trust-failure diagnosis and lock the build ground rules so the solution is built against the real problem.
stories.user_value: Prevents building the wrong gates: validates that aggregation/units/currency/truncation (not raw text fabrication) dominate the trust failure, and records the Python 3 stdlib + stubbed-access decisions.

stories.title: As an OKOA associate, I can invoke the acos-hypercore-ask skill and have my question routed to the right verification tier.
stories.user_value: A single discoverable entry point exists; the skill loads, exposes the NL command surface, and classifies the question (trivial-lookup vs report/aggregation/analysis).

stories.title: As a developer, I can read Hypercore data through a stable read-only contract that works on fixtures today and swaps to live later without touching callers.
stories.user_value: The whole skill is buildable/testable before API access; the live backend is isolated and stubbed; absence of credentials degrades to an explicit no-live-data state.

stories.title: As the verification pipeline, I can persist raw API truth and derive a token-efficient normalized view that always points back to its source.
stories.user_value: Provenance is structurally guaranteed: every normalized field carries a back-pointer to its Tier-1 raw response; the cache is the immutable source of truth.

stories.title: As a consumer of an answer, I can trust that any delivered value cites its exact raw source, or is refused.
stories.user_value: No value is delivered without a resolvable provenance binding; missing binding triggers refusal, not a guess.

stories.title: As the verification pipeline, I can mechanically reject incomplete, stale, schema-invalid, unreconciled, or over-trusted values.
stories.user_value: Six deterministic gates (schema, pagination-completeness, freshness, reconciliation, unit/currency normalization, single-source cap <= 0.7) catch the dominant non-text failure modes before delivery.

stories.title: As an IC-grade consumer, I get report/aggregation answers only when N blind independent agents agree on substance.
stories.user_value: Adversarial multi-model consensus catches substance disagreement on math/aggregations; disagreement re-dispatches then escalates, never a silent pick.

stories.title: As an OKOA associate, I can ask a single-value question and get a verified answer (or an explicit no-live-data message) against fixtures, with zero live API.
stories.user_value: Demo 1: the thin end-to-end deterministic-tier path proves a verified answer with full provenance/confidence display and the graceful no-live-data degradation.

stories.title: As an OKOA associate, I can ask a report/aggregation question and get a consensus-verified, gated, provenance-bound report/table.
stories.user_value: The full pipeline (router -> adapter -> cache -> normalize -> blind agents -> consensus -> gates -> binder -> deliver) produces an IC-grade report or refuses/escalates.

stories.title: As a downstream ACOS skill, I can consume a verified dataset with embedded provenance/confidence and a manifest as a trusted input.
stories.user_value: Demo 3: a verified dataset is exported in report/table/dataset (JSON/CSV) feed formats with a manifest and is consumed by a downstream skill (e.g. acos-dataroom-v2).

stories.title: As OKOA, I am assured sensitive loan data and credentials are handled safely and the adapter can never mutate Hypercore.
stories.user_value: PII-scrubbed logs/evidence, env/secret-store credentials, and a structural read-only guard make the skill safe to point at live data once provisioned.

stories.title: As an IC-grade consumer, lists and reports are pagination-complete, fresh, and drift-checked under stress.
stories.user_value: Hardens completeness/freshness/schema-drift handling with adversarial fixtures (deliberately truncated, stale, drifted) so the gates demonstrably catch the failure modes.

slices.objective: Confirm symptoms/unknowns, validate hypothesis H1, and record the Python 3 stdlib + stubbed-access decisions before any solution code.
Scaffold the acos-hypercore-ask skill (SKILL.md command surface) + config + tier-router entry point + evidence-bundle wiring.
Define the read-only Hypercore adapter contract with FixtureBackend (active) + stubbed LiveBackend + is_live()/NoLiveDataError degradation.
Implement the Tier-1 RawApiResponse cache (immutable source of truth) + Tier-2 NormalizedAnswerRecord derived view with per-field back-pointers.
Implement the provenance-binding engine that binds each value to its Tier-1 source and refuses delivery on any missing/unresolvable binding.
Implement the deterministic gate suite: schema, pagination-completeness, freshness, cross-field reconciliation, unit/currency normalization, single-source confidence cap <= 0.7.
Wire the thin end-to-end deterministic-tier path (NL -> stubbed client -> raw cache -> provenance-bound value -> gates -> display) plus the no-live-data degradation. Demo 1.
Implement the blind adversarial-consensus orchestrator: N general-purpose Task() agents, substance consensus, bounded re-dispatch then escalate, single-source cap. Demo 2.
Assemble the full question->plan->fetch->verify->answer orchestration in SKILL.md for the report/aggregation tier (router -> ... -> consensus -> gates -> binder -> deliver | refuse | escalate).
Render report/table/dataset (JSON/CSV) deliverables + the trusted-input feed schema (embedded provenance/confidence + manifest) and demonstrate downstream consumption. Demo 3.
Harden completeness/freshness/schema-drift with adversarial fixtures (truncated/stale/drifted) proving the gates catch each failure mode.
Harden security/PII/GDPR: PII-scrubbed logs/evidence, env/secret-store credential loading, and the structural read-only guard test.
